newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: MOTORCYCLING-CRIVILLE TAKES POLE AS DOOHAN STRUGGLES.
newsitem.headline: MOTORCYCLING-CRIVILLE TAKES POLE AS DOOHAN STRUGGLES.

text.p: Spaniard Alex
Criville took pole position on Saturday for Sunday's
season-ending Australian motorcycling grand prix but
newly-crowned world 500cc champion Michael Doohan struggled with
suspension problems.
Criville denied his Honda team mate a fourth successive pole
position despite being unable to improve on his time of one
minute 30.478 seconds from the first qualifying session on
Friday.
"I couldn't go any faster today but I am very happy with the
bike and the tyres are working well," said Criville, who has
already secured second place in the riders' championship.
Doohan, who sealed his third consecutive world championship
crown last month with two races to spare, also failed to go
below his time of one minute 30.589 seconds from Friday and
takes third place on the grid.
"We will be changing the front and rear suspension for the
warm-up session on Sunday before the race. I just couldn't get
any grip today and the bike was moving about a bit," said
Doohan.
"(But) I still think both myself and Alex are going to be
strong and it will be up to the other guys to take it to us on
Sunday," Doohan said of his main rival this season.
Italian Loris Capirossi, riding a Yamaha, took advantage of
Doohan's troubles to qualify second fastest with an improved
time of one minute 30.553 seconds in dry, blustery conditions at
the 3.93-km circuit on the outskirts of Sydney.
Doohan, winner of eight grands prix in 14 starts this
season, said he was looking forward to a break from racing.
"It's like the last day in the office before being allowed
to go on holiday. It's no different from any other day but you
do look forward to it being over," Doohan said.
